title: Read-only native Taskfleet children and the selected worker's conversation

state.description: working: Taskfleet runs the worker and its agent is at work. idle: Taskfleet still runs it, but the worker's own Pi session says its turn ended and it waits at its prompt for a person (an interactive run waiting for review, or a worker that stopped without finishing). waiting_parent: it waits for the conversation that started it: an interactive run Taskfleet says needs attention, or a named worker between rounds (resident).

preserved.description: The ended run's branch or worktree is still on disk. In the list (no run query) an ended run appears only while this holds.

harness.description: The worker's agent: Pi, Claude Code, or another Taskfleet harness.

other_repository.description: The directory name of the worker's repository, present only when the parent conversation does not run inside it.

ended_at.description: When an ended run's Taskfleet manifest was last written, which is when it ended; absent while it runs.

awaiting_input.description: The worker waits for input at its own terminal prompt: Taskfleet reads it so, or the worker's Pi has run for a minute without sending the task it was started with (a startup question such as Pi's project trust prompt holds it; the state is then idle).

terminal.description: The live worker's Taskfleet window and, when Taskfleet recorded it, the agent's pane in it, as the browser shell's read-only token (terminal.schema.json); only for the selected run, and only a pointer the terminal route checks again.

brief.description: The task Taskfleet gave the worker (its run's prompt); only for the selected run.

resident.description: A named support worker (Taskfleet resident run): it works in rounds, reports each, and waits for the main agent's next message, which resumes the same session. Taskfleet's own round state; absent for an ordinary worker.

name.description: Its Taskfleet name, which the main agent messages it by.

round_state.description: working: a round is under way. waiting: it reported its round and waits for the main agent. dormant: it waited past Taskfleet's idle expiry with everything landed, so Taskfleet removed its worktree; the next message brings it back. Meaningful only while the run is live.

report.description: Its latest round report, the worker's own words.

landed_round.description: The latest round Taskfleet landed into the source branch.

unlanded.description: Taskfleet's idle expiry found work not yet landed and kept it on the worker's branch.

git_workspace.description: The opaque ID under which the workspace Git routes read the worker's worktree: a Git workspace of its own or a worktree place of one (ADR 0025), as Git's own registry names it. Only for the selected run, only while its worktree is on disk and registered; the route resolves it again on every read.

terminal_workspace.description: The workspace whose terminal route lists that window: the one holding the worker's worktree, which may be another than the parent's. Present exactly with terminal.

availability.description: available: the worker's native session was read. unavailable: not found (yet) or not readable. unsupported: Habitat reads no history of this harness.

entries.description: The newest part of the worker's native conversation as history entries. Tool-call arguments are inline (bounded); no block is read on demand.
